title: Interactive JointJS Diagrams
text: package uses R6 class objects create graphs define elements: Widget Preview Example Note page render interactive diagrams. Therefore, shows static screenshot widget generated code chunk.
code: library(jointjs) graph <-   jointjs_graph$   ## Create a new graph:   new()$   ## Add elements:   add_elements(     ## Add a rectangle:     jointjs_rectangle$new(id = "hello")$       set_body(rx = 5, ry = 5)$       set_label("Hello")$       set_position(10, 10),     ## Add a circle:     jointjs_circle$new(id = "world")$       set_label("world")$       set_body("white", "black")$       set_position(100, 10),     ## Add a link, joining the rectangle and circle:     jointjs_doubleLink$new(list(id = "hello"), list(id = "world"))   ) ## Get and show widget: my_widget <- graph$get_widget(width = 170, height = 70)

title: Interactive JointJS Diagrams
text: dagitty free web-based application matching R package used draw, edit, analyze causal diagrams. diagram Plots networks transition matrices plots food webs. focuses R base plots. DiagrammeR: Build manipulate nodes edges programmatically using R syntax specialized text languages. Supports DOT language create diagrams. ggdag wrapper around dagitty allows add graph layers ggplots. ggraph standard ggplot2 users. treats nodes edges standard ggplot layers (geom_node_point(), geom_edge_link()), allowing use familiar themes, scales, facets network data. igraph Essential network analysis R. primarily used computing graph mathematics (centrality, paths), includes robust base-R plotting capabilities (plot.igraph) traditional network rendering. networkD3 Creates interactive force-directed graphs node-link diagrams using D3.js. excellent quick, clean, responsive web animations minimal code. sigmajs interface Sigma.js library, specifically optimized rendering massive, complex graphs smoothly using WebGL. visNetwork Uses vis.js JavaScript library create highly interactive, customisable network graphs. can drag nodes, zoom, filter, animate networks.

title: Create an Interactive JointJS Diagram — jointjs
code: if (interactive()) {   graph <-     jointjs_graph$new()$       add_elements(         jointjs_rectangle$new(id = "hello", label = list(text = "Hello"))$           set_position(5, 5),         jointjs_circle$new(id = "world", label = list(text = "World"))$           set_position(70, 5),         jointjs_doubleLink$new(source = list(id = "hello"),                                target = list(id = "world"))       )   jointjs(graph = graph) }
